close_reason: Already fixed by bd:JMAP-qz9v.2 (commit 4f64602). handle_contact_card_copy now rejects same-account /copy with invalidArguments matching the canonical mail-server pattern. Test copy_same_account_rejected_with_invalid_arguments locks in the fix.
description:
This is a duplicate detail-issue split out of JMAP-qz9v.2 specifically to capture the simplest immediate fix. RFC 8620 §5.4: 'The id of the account to copy records to. This MUST be different to the fromAccountId.'

Trigger:
  ContactCard/copy { accountId: 'acc1', fromAccountId: 'acc1', create: { c1: { id: 'card1' } } }

Current behavior: handler at card.rs:345 accepts both ids, fetches the card from acc1, calls copy_contact_card(from='acc1', to='acc1', card), MemoryBackend mints a new id in the same account, and now there are two copies of the same card in one account.

Spec-correct behavior: return JmapError::invalid_arguments('accountId must be different from fromAccountId') at the top of handle_contact_card_copy, before any state queries.

The canonical mail-server enforces this at email.rs:2263-2268. A one-line check in card.rs that mirrors that pattern closes the gap. Sibling-divergence regression per the canonical-template rule.

Test gap: no test covers the same-account case. Adding one would lock in the fix.
title: ContactCard/copy permits accountId == fromAccountId with no error — should be invalidArguments per RFC 8620 §5.4
